title: Cobalt watch transition brief — 2027-07-18
content:
Shift window: 2027-07-18 07:00 UTC -> 2027-07-18 15:00 UTC
Severity posture: Green -> brief yellow for a transient token-cache regression at 10:12 UTC that resolved to degraded p95 for ~11 minutes. No customer-facing errors recorded.

TL;DR
- Primary event: token-cache evictions caused a short-lived p95 spike (350ms -> 760ms) between 10:12–10:23 UTC. Root cause appears to be an autoscaler mis-sync on a small Dedicated pool after a scheduled config roll.
- Impact: internal retriable latency only; small subset of Dedicated capacity experienced higher tail latency. No 5xx increase; overall request success rate stayed >99.98%.
- Status: Recoveries performed, temporary mitigations deployed. Long-term follow-ups assigned.

Incidents and timeline
- 10:11 UTC — Alert: p95 latency for model-runner-prod-dedicated-3 crossed 600ms (alert: SRE-p95-latency-threshold). Pager triggered.
- 10:12 UTC — On-call (Evelyn) acknowledged. Started quick triage: checked autoscaler events, node eviction logs, and KV-cache metrics.
- 10:15 UTC — Observed increased cache miss rate and eviction spikes on pool dedicated-3. An in-progress config rollout (cloud-agent 1.9.3 -> 1.9.4) was noted in rollout audit.
- 10:17 UTC — Applied temporary routing policy to shift new requests away from dedicated-3 to dedicated-2 for models: gpt-redwood-3b and gpt-redwood-7b.
- 10:20 UTC — Scaled dedicated-3 by +1 replica manually to relieve pressure while rollback plan prepared.
- 10:22 UTC — Root cause narrowed to a bug in the agent that double-counted cache shards during rolling restart, causing unexpected memory pressure and evictions.
- 10:23 UTC — p95 returned to baseline after manual scale and routing; alert auto-resolved at 10:24 UTC.

Mitigations performed (short-term)
- Manual replica bump (+1) for dedicated-3.
- Temporary routing rule to prefer dedicated-2 for traffic to affected model families (applied via routing console; change id: ROUTE-79321).
- Increased alert sensitivity window to avoid alert fatigue while we validate runbook deltas (temporarily adjusted in alerting config: ALRT-350-temp).

Runbook deltas / notes to update runbook
- Add a check to the rolling-restart playbook to validate cache-shard ownership metric post-upgrade (metric: cache.shard.ownership.diff). Fail rollout if diff > 0.02 for 2 consecutive mins.
- Explicit step to validate cloud-agent version compatibility with cache manager prior to rolling restarts for Dedicated pools.
- Add a one-liner CLI snippet to routing runbook for quick route-weight adjustments: `ri route-set --pool dedicated-3 --weight 0.1` (for fast traffic diversion).
- Update escalation matrix: include Platform Release Lead (Mateo Ruiz) earlier during rolling upgrades when capacity-sensitive pools are touched.

Action items and owners (post-shift)
- Priority: Patch and release cloud-agent fix that prevents double-counting shards. Owner: Mateo Ruiz. Target: 2027-07-22 (code + canary).
- Add automated post-rollout cache-consistency check to deployment pipeline. Owner: Jun Ho Kim. Target: 2027-07-21.
- Create a lightweight smoke test to exercise KV cache on every node immediately after restart. Owner: Priya Singh. Target: 2027-07-20.
- Update SRE runbook (Cobalt watch) with above deltas and doc the CLI route commands. Owner: Evelyn Park. Target: 2027-07-19.
- Postmortem candidate: Evaluate whether this meets threshold for full postmortem (SRE-1245). Owner: Evelyn Park. Decision due 2027-07-19.

Monitoring snapshot (at 11:00 UTC)
- aggregate p95 (global) for text-gen endpoints: 210ms (baseline ~200ms)
- error rate (5xx): 0.02%
- Dedicated pool dedicated-3 memory used: 78% -> stabilized at 55% after scale
- cache eviction rate: peaked 1200 evictions/min -> baseline ~20 evictions/min
- active connections on dedicated-3: 820 -> normalized to 610 after routing change

Escalation contacts used
- Platform Release Lead: Mateo Ruiz (paged at 10:18 UTC) — responded 10:25 UTC
- Lead SRE oncall (backup): Jun Ho Kim — available for kernel-level investigations
- Product owner for Dedicated: Sara Al-Mansour (notified via Slack thread #prod-dedicated)

Notes to next shift (handing off)
- Running tasks: follow-ups above (patch + pipeline checks + smoke test). Expect small follow-ups on canary results once patch lands.
- Temporary routing rule remains in place with 10% traffic to dedicated-3; plan to remove when canary shows stable cache metrics for 24h.
- If evictions spike again, escalation path: notify Platform Release Lead -> pause any active rollouts on dedicated pools -> move traffic away and scale as needed.
- Dashboard links: Latency dashboard (short): https://grafana.redwood.company/d/latency/cobalt-short?orgId=1
  Cache metrics: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/cache/cobalt-cache?orgId=1

Quick CLI snippets (for reference)
- Inspect agent rollout state: `ri infra agent-status --pool dedicated-3 --filter rollout`
- Force route diversion: `ri route-set --pool dedicated-3 --weight 0.1 --reason \"handoff mitigation\"`
- Check cache shard diff: `ri metrics query \"cache.shard.ownership.diff{pool=\\\"dedicated-3\\\"}\" --window 2m`

Open questions / unresolved
- Why did the rollout system not mark the rollout as unhealthy earlier? (Investigation ticket SRE-1248)
- Are there other pools with older agent binaries where the same bug could exist? Quick inventory requested (SRE-1250).

Post-shift handoff checklist (tick when done)
- [ ] Confirm all action-item owners accept tasks in JIRA (Evelyn -> verify by 09:00 UTC 2027-07-19)
- [ ] Publish runbook updates to Confluence and link in slack #sre-runbooks
- [ ] Remove temporary alert sensitivity adjustment after runbook validated
- [ ] Re-run smoke test against dedicated-3 once patch is live

Appendix: Relevant logs and excerpts (copied into incident archive)
- Excerpt: `2027-07-18T10:16:37Z agent[pid=4212] WARN cache: shard-count mismatch (expected 128, observed 129) -> triggering eviction cycle`
- Excerpt: `2027-07-18T10:18:02Z routing-service INFO reroute applied: pool=dedicated-3 weight=0.1 id=ROUTE-79321`

If any questions while taking over, ping @evelyn on #sre-ops or page on-call using SRE rotation.

End of brief.
